checkpoints: Compile the public Java sources with OpenJDK 11 after any Action; VISIBLE_CHECKS.md says compilation is required but does not establish business behavior.
Verify each terminal path requests cleanup once: first match, end of source, cancelled read, and predicate failure.
Verify the returned completion remains pending while asynchronous cleanup is pending, then retains the original terminal outcome after successful cleanup.
Verify unmatched records still cause strictly sequential reads and no read begins after a terminal condition.
forbidden_effects: Do not change the documented Environment or Controller call interfaces.
Do not reorder, skip, or concurrently scan records.
Do not allow a terminal path to request cleanup more than once.
Do not start another read after a match, exhaustion, cancellation, or predicate failure is observed.
Do not report successful completion, cancellation, or predicate failure before required asynchronous cleanup has completed successfully.
Do not change unrelated start, cancel, snapshot, dispose, output, or result-shaping behavior.
lifecycle_identity: A Controller owns the retained asynchronous source associated with its existing Environment and key.
All next and close operations for a scan must use that same Environment and key.
The completion created by start represents the scan lifecycle and must not be treated as resource cleanup; the producer is retained independently of the consumer.
The existing finishing guard identifies the single terminal transition and should protect cleanup and acknowledgement from duplication.

obligations.text: Repair Controller's record scan so its owned retained asynchronous source is closed on every observed terminal path: first match, source exhaustion, cancelled read, and predicate failure.
Because close is asynchronous and may suspend, do not acknowledge the scan's terminal outcome until successful cleanup completes.
Preserve scan order: request one next record at a time, evaluate records in source order, and request another record only after the current record is nonterminal and does not match.

Preserve terminal outcomes after successful cleanup: a match returns that record value, exhaustion returns null, a cancelled read completes with CancellationException, and a predicate failure completes exceptionally with the original failure.
Ensure the terminal transition and close request occur at most once for a scan, including when asynchronous callbacks arrive after termination.
Keep the documented public interfaces and unrelated behavior, and use only the Java standard library.

ordering_barriers: Each next operation must complete before its row is inspected and before any subsequent next operation begins.
Predicate evaluation for the current row must finish before deciding whether to read another row or enter termination.
Once a terminal condition is observed, close must be requested before terminal acknowledgement.
When close remains pending, terminal acknowledgement must remain pending because cleanup may suspend.
After successful close completion, acknowledge exactly the terminal result already selected; cleanup must not change scan order or replace a predicate failure.
preservation: Records are inspected in source order until the first match.
The first matching value is returned; exhaustion returns null.
The configured predicate failure remains an error with its existing exception identity and message.
A row marked cancelled remains cancellation rather than normal completion.
The existing cancel call continues to emit cancelInput through Environment.
The Environment methods and Controller call names and result/snapshot shapes remain unchanged unless cleanup timing necessarily delays their done state.
Only src/Workflow.java business code is in scope for a later Action; tests and configuration must remain untouched.
scope: Controller's asynchronous scan and terminal cleanup behavior in src/Workflow.java.
The retained record source accessed through Environment.resolve("next", key, null) and Environment.resolve("close", key, null).
No workspace modification is part of this Contract-drafting stage.
